GAME TIME

Basketball School

### I-ON-I BLIND SHOOTING

16 MIN BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Players find a partner and a ball. Three groups can play 1-on-1 on the same basket at the same time. The defender will start 'blind' to the offense, with their heels on the 3PT line facing the basket. The offense will hold the ball and place it on the defender's back. Once they lift the ball from the defense's back, it becomes a live 1-on-1. The offense has a maximum of three dribbles to score but can only score by shooting outside the paint. Each repetition should have a different starting location, beginning anywhere outside the paint.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating and maintaining advantage
- Attempting to shoot as quickly and controlled as possible
- Exploring different ways to stop (e.g. jump stop, stride stop, etc).

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The defense is not allowed to block the shooter, but can distract them.
- The offense and defense must change partners after they both play offense.
- The offense can only score with one dribble.
- The offense gets double points for a swish.
- The offense begins in the paint, facing away from the basket, and must escape the lava and shoot within three dribbles.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Get the players organized to read the space and successfully organize themselves by communicating whose turn it is.
- Challenge players to get their shot off quickly before the defender can recover.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can you use the space before the defense can recover?"
- "How can the defense rear view contest without fouling?"

Load for younger players

4-ON-4 DEFENSIVE SHUTDOWN

20 MIN BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of four. Make sure each basket has a minimum of three teams and a maximum of six. Teams will play continuous half-court 4-on-4 with additional teams waiting at the half-court area. If a defensive stop is secured (defensive rebound or forced turnover), the defense gets 2 points and stays on defense while a new offense comes on from the half-court area (the old offense team rotates off to the end of the line). If the offense scores, they rotate to defense and play against a new team on offense (the old defense team rotates off to the end of the line).

#### SCORING

Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Pressuring the ball with intensity
- Helping and stopping the ball
- Disrupting the offense with double teams

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The defense must always ensure there is adequate ball pressure: the on-ball defender must be within arm's distance from the offensive player.
- The defense must avoid fouling.
- The defense achieves an extra 2 points for any successful trap (double team) which leads to a turnover.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Send off defense when lapses happen (inadequate ball pressure, foul, etc.).
- Emphasize and teach defensive concepts and philosophy.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "What does good ball pressure look like?"
- "What are the best scenarios to trap?""

MODULE 2: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

5-ON-5 LOADS-BASED

20 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of five players, based on the number of courts available. Try to have a maximum of five teams on each full-court. In instances of very high numbers, half-courts can be used. Teams play to three baskets. After a team scores three baskets, they get 1 point. The losing team will rotate off while the next team waiting rotates on. The game is then continually played, with teams keeping track of their total number of points over the course of the activity.

#### SCORING

3 baskets = 1 point for team.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Maintaining good spacing
- Hunting out open shots

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can you get the most efficient shot?"
- "How can we help teammates emphasize continuous ball pressure?"
- "What can you do to space the floor effectively?"

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Play 4-on-4, with a +1 who is always on offense.
- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- Escape the lava. After a pass or cut is completed, the offensive player without the ball has three seconds to escape the lava (space out outside the 3PT line). If they are still inside after three seconds, a turnover is called.
- Pass and cut is a turnover. Players can only create an advantage through a static 1-on-1 where the ball-handler creates an advantage with a dribble move from the perimeter, or through a post-up. Teammates should maintain spacing (following the 'lava' load), ready to receive the ball.
- Double teams that lead to turnovers result in an extra 3 points.
- No ball pressure results in the defensive team losing 1 point and the offense regaining possession on the sideline.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Organize the waiting teams on the sideline so teams transition quickly for the next repetition.
- Ensure players substitute every few minutes.
- Emphasize and teach offensive and defensive concepts and philosophy.
